## File: `references/languages/python.md`

### Detection signals — Python (Security: Operational)

Detection signals only. They cite no standard. Report findings against the element IDs listed (defined in
`../standards/`). A signal is evidence only on concrete code or an explicit setting (`SKILL.md` step 4). The only
Python defaults a worker may rely on are those stated in `python-operational.md` (PYO-01, PYO-03, PYO-05, PYO-08).
Flask, FastAPI, `python-dotenv`, structlog and loguru defaults are not localized: report explicit values only, and add
a `localized-standard-gap` note for a missing setting.

| Signal (API, setting or pattern) | Look in | Indicates | Element(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEBUG = True` in production settings; `DEBUG = os.environ.get("DEBUG", True)`-style truthy defaults | `settings*.py`, env templates | Production debug mode (always Error) | PYO-01 |
| Flask `app.run(debug=True)`, `app.debug = True`, `FLASK_DEBUG=1` in production config | app factory, Dockerfile, env files | Debug mode (Flask defaults not localized: add a gap note for missing settings) | ERR-04 |
| One `settings.py` with development values and no per-environment split | `settings*.py` | Environments not separated | SCR-02, SCR-01 |
| Literal `SECRET_KEY = "…"` | `settings*.py` | Hardcoded Django key | PYO-02 |
| Committed `.env` with real values; literal passwords/API keys in `settings*.py`/`config.py` | repository root, settings | Hardcoded secrets (`python-dotenv` itself is not a finding) | SMG-01 |
| Production settings with no `LOGGING` and no `ADMINS` | `settings*.py` | Server errors not logged anywhere visible | PYO-05 |
| `AdminEmailHandler` with `include_html: True` | `LOGGING` | Locals and settings mailed | PYO-04 |
| Login, password-change or payment views without `@sensitive_variables`/`@sensitive_post_parameters` | `views.py` | Secrets in error reports | PYO-03 |
| `except Exception: pass`, bare `except:` without logging | any code | Swallowed errors | A10-07, LOG-02 |
| `return JsonResponse({"error": str(e)})`, `traceback.format_exc()` in responses | views, API handlers | Error details sent to clients | ERR-02 |
| No `handler500` or error middleware where views return exception details | `urls.py`, middleware | No global generic handler | ERR-01 |
| `logger.info(f"…{x}")`, `logger.info("…%s" % x)`, `.format()` into logger calls | any code | Pre-formatted log messages | PYO-09, LOG-17 |
| Passwords, tokens, `request.headers`, `request.POST`, `request.body` logged | any code | Secrets or sensitive data in logs | LOG-12, LOG-13 |
| `logging.config.fileConfig`/`dictConfig` on paths or data from requests or uploads | any code | Untrusted logging configuration | PYO-06 |
| `logging.config.listen(` without `verify` | any code | Configuration via `eval()` | PYO-07 |
| Custom handlers that re-raise from `emit()`; `logging.raiseExceptions = True` set in production code | logging modules | Logging failures break the app | PYO-08, LOG-20 |
| `FileHandler` without rotation; `RotatingFileHandler(maxBytes=0)`; log files under `STATIC_ROOT`/`MEDIA_ROOT` | `LOGGING`, logging modules | Unbounded or web-accessible log files | LOG-21, LOG-22 |
| `SysLogHandler` over UDP or `HTTPHandler` with `secure=False` across networks | `LOGGING` | Logs in plaintext transit | LOG-24 |
| Security events written with `print` | admin, export, management commands | Not using the logging framework | LOG-11 |
| Permission checks that `return True` in `except` | permissions, decorators, middleware | Fail open | A10-05 |
| Multi-step ORM writes without `transaction.atomic()` | services, views | No rollback for part-way writes | A10-03, SCR-03 |
| File handles, sockets or locks without `with`/`finally` | any code | Resources not released on exceptions | A10-06 |

## File: `references/standards/python-operational.md`

*Load rule: PYO-01…09. Load when language `python` is detected.*

### Python / Django operational security guidance — localized summary

- Applies when language `python` is detected. Django elements (PYO-01 … PYO-05) apply when `Django` is a dependency;
  CPython `logging` elements (PYO-06 … PYO-09) always.
- Level: a vendor element takes the level of the OWASP element it supports, or `SHOULD` when the vendor only
  recommends. **(Default)** marks an element that states API behaviour or a default; cite the OWASP element it supports
  and name the PYO element in the recommendation. Where vendor guidance is weaker than an OWASP element, the OWASP
  element decides. Severity rules are in `../../SKILL.md`.
- Defaults stated here are the only Python defaults a worker may rely on. Flask (`debug`, `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS`),
  FastAPI exception handlers, `python-dotenv`, structlog and loguru defaults are **not** localized: report only explicit
  insecure settings there (e.g. `app.run(debug=True)` fails ERR-04), and add a `localized-standard-gap` note for a
  missing setting.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PYO-01 | MUST | Never run production with `DEBUG = True`. The default is `False`, but `startproject` sets `True`. Debug pages expose tracebacks, environment metadata and settings (only names containing API, KEY, PASS, SECRET, SIGNATURE or TOKEN are hidden), and debug mode keeps every SQL query in memory. | `DEBUG = True` in production settings; `DEBUG` defaulting to `True` from env | SEC-OP-07 |
| PYO-02 | MUST | `SECRET_KEY` is a large random value, kept secret, not reused, not committed; load it from an environment variable or file; remove old keys from `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` promptly. | literal `SECRET_KEY = "…"` in settings | SEC-OP-05 |
| PYO-03 | SHOULD | **(Default)** Error reports include the full traceback, each frame's local variables and request attributes. Use `sensitive_variables()` and `sensitive_post_parameters()` on views handling passwords, card numbers or similar. | login/payment views without the decorators | SEC-OP-03 |
| PYO-04 | SHOULD | Error reports go only to trusted team members and aren't sent unencrypted; avoid `AdminEmailHandler(include_html=True)`, which mails locals and settings. | `include_html: True` in `LOGGING` | SEC-OP-03 |
| PYO-05 | MUST | **(Default)** With `DEBUG = False`, the default config sends `django` ERROR/CRITICAL records only to `AdminEmailHandler` (requires `ADMINS`); the console handler requires `DEBUG = True`. Review `LOGGING` before production. | production settings with no `LOGGING` and no `ADMINS` | SEC-OP-02 |
| PYO-06 | MUST | Never load logging configuration (`fileConfig`, `dictConfig`) from untrusted sources: it can import and call arbitrary code. | config path or dict taken from request/user input | SEC-OP-09 |
| PYO-07 | SHOULD | Avoid `logging.config.listen()` on hosts with untrusted local users, or pass a `verify` callable: received configuration goes through `eval()`. | `logging.config.listen(` without `verify` | SEC-OP-09 |
| PYO-08 | SHOULD | **(Default)** `logging.raiseExceptions` defaults to `True` (handler errors print tracebacks to stderr); set it to `False` in production. Handler errors are otherwise swallowed so logging can't terminate the app. | custom handlers that re-raise from `emit()` | SEC-OP-09 |
| PYO-09 | SHOULD | Log variable data as a format string plus arguments (`logger.info("user %s", uid)`), not pre-formatted strings. | f-strings or `%`-formatted strings passed to logger calls | SEC-OP-04 |
